claim: Gli2f/f;Gli3f/f;Wnt1-Cre conditional mutant mice present with mid-facial widening, cleft lip/palate, and a domed cranial vault.
source: While these mutants present with a variety of cranial defects including mid-facial widening, cleft lip/palate (Chang et al., 2016) and a domed cranial vault; we also observed a severe micrognathic phenotype in Gli2/3 cKO embryos.
evidence: The manuscript describes observed phenotypes in conditional knockout mice with citation to prior work.

claim: Gli2f/f;Gli3f/f;Wnt1-Cre conditional mutant mice exhibit severe micrognathia.
source: While these mutants present with a variety of cranial defects including mid-facial widening, cleft lip/palate (Chang et al., 2016) and a domed cranial vault; we also observed a severe micrognathic phenotype in Gli2/3 cKO embryos.
evidence: The manuscript reports observed phenotypes in conditional knockout mice.

claim: Gli2/3 cKO mutants present with low-set pinnae, aglossia and micrognathia relative to wild-type embryos.
source: Relative to wild-type embryos, Gli2/3 cKO mutants presented with low-set pinnae, aglossia and micrognathia (Figure 1A–C', I).
evidence: The manuscript describes phenotypes observed in mutant embryos and references supporting figures.

claim: The distal mandible in Gli2/3 cKO mutants is hypoplastic with absent incisors.
source: While the distal mandible was hypoplastic and certain distal structures such as the incisors were absent, the proximal mandible was more severely affected.
evidence: The manuscript describes anatomical defects observed in mutant embryos.

claim: Proximal mandibular structures including the coronoid, condylar, and angular processes are almost completely lost in Gli2/3 cKO mutants.
source: Proximal mandibular structures such as the coronoid, condylar, and angular processes, were almost completely lost (Figure 1D,I, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–B) and posterior cranial skeletal structures including the tympanic ring were hypoplastic.
evidence: The manuscript describes anatomical defects with reference to supporting figures.

claim: Posterior cranial skeletal structures including the tympanic ring are hypoplastic in Gli2/3 cKO mutants.
source: Proximal mandibular structures such as the coronoid, condylar, and angular processes, were almost completely lost (Figure 1D,I, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–B) and posterior cranial skeletal structures including the tympanic ring were hypoplastic.
evidence: The manuscript describes anatomical defects with reference to supporting figures.

claim: Conditional loss of either Gli2 or Gli3 alone does not replicate the mandibular phenotype observed in double mutants.
source: Interestingly, conditional loss of either Gli2 or Gli3 alone (Gli2f/f;Wnt1-Cre or Gli3f/f;Wnt1-Cre) did not replicate the mandibular phenotype observed in double mutants (Chang et al., 2016).
evidence: The manuscript reports genetic analysis results with citation to prior work.

claim: Hand2f/f;Wnt1-Cre mutants present with low-set pinnae, aglossia and micrognathia, similar to Gli2/3 cKO embryos.
source: While Hand2f/f;Wnt1-Cre mutants (herein referred to as Hand2 cKO) did not present with mid-facial, clefting or calvarial phenotypes, they did present with low-set pinnae, aglossia and micrognathia, similar to Gli2/3 cKO embryos (Figure 1E–E', I; Morikawa et al., 2007; Barron et al., 2011).
evidence: The manuscript describes observed phenotypes with citations to prior work and reference to supporting figures.

claim: Hand2 cKO mutants exhibit a dysmorphic and hypoplastic mandible and loss of Meckel's cartilage.
source: Skeletal analysis of Hand2 cKO mutants confirmed a dysmorphic and hypoplastic mandible and loss of Meckel's cartilage (Figure 1F,I).
evidence: The manuscript reports skeletal analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: Hand2 cKO embryos exhibit a less severe proximal mandibular phenotype compared to Gli2/3 cKO embryos.
source: Compared to the Gli2/3 cKO embryos, Hand2 cKO embryos exhibited a less severe proximal mandibular phenotype.
evidence: The manuscript compares phenotypes between different mutant lines.

claim: In Hand2 cKO embryos, the tympanic ring and angular processes are absent, while the coronoid and condylar processes are not severely hypoplastic.
source: While the tympanic ring and angular processes were absent, the coronoid and condylar processes were not severely hypoplastic (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The manuscript describes anatomical observations with reference to supporting figures.

claim: The hyoid bone in Hand2 cKO mutants is present but abnormally fused to middle ear cartilage and undergoes excessive/ectopic ossification.
source: Although the hyoid bone was present, it was abnormally fused to middle ear cartilage and underwent excessive/ectopic ossification (Barron et al., 2011).
evidence: The manuscript describes anatomical observations with citation to prior work.

claim: Hand2 cKO mutants exhibit extreme distal jaw hypoplasia.
source: Most strikingly; however, the Hand2 cKO mutants exhibited extreme distal jaw hypoplasia.
evidence: The manuscript describes observed phenotypes in mutant embryos.

claim: Gli2 and Gli3 are predominantly required for proximal jaw development.
source: Together, these phenotypic analyses suggested that while Gli2 and Gli3 were predominantly required for proximal jaw development and Hand2 was predominantly required for distal jaw development, both Gli2/3 and Hand2 were necessary for proper mandibular development.
evidence: The manuscript interprets phenotypic data to infer functional roles.

claim: Hand2 is predominantly required for distal jaw development.
source: Together, these phenotypic analyses suggested that while Gli2 and Gli3 were predominantly required for proximal jaw development and Hand2 was predominantly required for distal jaw development, both Gli2/3 and Hand2 were necessary for proper mandibular development.
evidence: The manuscript interprets phenotypic data to infer functional roles.

claim: Both Gli2/3 and Hand2 are necessary for proper mandibular development.
source: Together, these phenotypic analyses suggested that while Gli2 and Gli3 were predominantly required for proximal jaw development and Hand2 was predominantly required for distal jaw development, both Gli2/3 and Hand2 were necessary for proper mandibular development.
evidence: The manuscript interprets phenotypic data to infer functional roles.

claim: Hand2 expression is not significantly changed in Gli2/3 cKO MNPs.
source: We analyzed gene expression in both conditional KO mutant embryos by RNA-seq and did not detect significant changes in expression of Hand2 in Gli2/3 cKO MNPs, or significant changes in the expression of Shh pathway components in Hand2 cKO MNPs (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports RNA-seq analysis results.

claim: Shh pathway components are not significantly changed in Hand2 cKO MNPs.
source: We analyzed gene expression in both conditional KO mutant embryos by RNA-seq and did not detect significant changes in expression of Hand2 in Gli2/3 cKO MNPs, or significant changes in the expression of Shh pathway components in Hand2 cKO MNPs (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports RNA-seq analysis results.

claim: Gli TFs and Hand2 may work in parallel to promote MNP patterning and development, rather than functioning up or downstream of one another.
source: Thus, in contrast to the limb (Vokes et al., 2008), these data suggest that rather than functioning up or downstream of one another, these TFs may work in parallel to promote MNP patterning and development.
evidence: The manuscript interprets RNA-seq data and compares to prior work in the limb.

claim: Triple heterozygous mutants (Hand2f/+;Gli2f/+;Gli3f/+;Wnt1-Cre) result in subtle yet significant MNP phenotypes, including low-set pinnae, micrognathia, smaller incisors, and hypoglossia.
source: First, while heterozygous Gli2/3 or Hand2 conditional mutants (Gli2f/+;Gli3f/+;Wnt1-Cre or Hand2f/+;Wnt1-Cre, respectively) did not produce significant MNP phenotypes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E–F'), triple heterozygotes (Hand2f/+;Gli2f/+;Gli3f/+;Wnt1-Cre) resulted in subtle yet significant MNP phenotypes, including low-set pinnae, micrognathia, smaller incisors, and hypoglossia (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G–H', I).
evidence: The manuscript reports genetic analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: Triple homozygous mutants (Gli2f/f;Gli3f/f;Hand2f/f;Wnt1-Cre) present with the most severe and significant lower jaw phenotypes when compared to all other combinatorial mutants.
source: Further, triple homozygous mutants (Gli2f/f;Gli3f/f;Hand2f/f;Wnt1-Cre) presented with the most severe and significant lower jaw phenotypes when compared to all other combinatorial mutants, including low-set pinnae, aglossia and a complete loss of both proximal and distal MNP structures (Figure 1G–I, Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The manuscript reports genetic analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: Hand2 physically interacts with both full-length and truncated isoforms of Gli3.
source: Hand2 physically interacted with both full-length and truncated isoforms of Gli3, but only the truncated isoform of Gli2 (Figure 1J, Figure 1—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: The manuscript reports co-immunoprecipitation results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: Hand2 physically interacts with only the truncated isoform of Gli2.
source: Hand2 physically interacted with both full-length and truncated isoforms of Gli3, but only the truncated isoform of Gli2 (Figure 1J, Figure 1—figure supplement 1J).
evidence: The manuscript reports co-immunoprecipitation results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: No spatial distinction or opposing expression gradients are observed between Gli2 and Gli3 in the developing MNP.
source: Contrary to the distinct and opposing Gli2 and Gli3 expression domains observed in other developing organ systems (Lee et al., 1997; Sasaki et al., 1997; Büscher and Rüther, 1998; Lei et al., 2004), no spatial distinction or opposing expression gradients were observed between Gli2 and Gli3 in the developing MNP (Figure 2A–C').
evidence: The manuscript reports expression analysis results with citations to prior work and reference to supporting figures.

claim: Gli2 and Gli3 are co-expressed within many cells of the developing MNP.
source: Furthermore, Gli2 and Gli3 were co-expressed within many cells of the developing MNP (Figure 2C–C'), supporting the hypothesis that the developing MNP uses unique mechanisms to integrate spatiotemporal information.
evidence: The manuscript reports expression analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: Hand2 expression is confined to the medial aspect of the MNP.
source: As opposed to the widespread MNP expression of Gli3 and Gli2, Hand2 expression was confined to the medial aspect of the MNP (Figure 2D–E; Srivastava et al., 1997; Thomas et al., 1998; Barron et al., 2011; Funato et al., 2016).
evidence: The manuscript reports expression analysis results with citations to prior work and reference to supporting figures.

claim: Most or all Hand2+ cells co-express Gli3.
source: Interestingly, while many Gli3+ cells did not express Hand2, most or all Hand2+ cells co-express Gli3 (Figure 2F,F').
evidence: The manuscript reports expression analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: At E11.5, there are over 2-fold more cells expressing Gli3 compared to Gli2 (1006 cells, 14.2% vs., 440 cells, 6.2%).
source: Coincident with RNAscope, Gli2 and Gli3 expression were not restricted to, nor enriched in any particular cell cluster. While we failed to observe a gradient or polarized expression of Gli TFs throughout the MNP, there were over 2-fold more cells expressing Gli3 compared to Gli2 (Figures 2H–I, 1006 cells, 14.2% vs., 440 cells, 6.2%).
evidence: The manuscript reports single-cell RNA-seq analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: 43% of cells expressing Hand2 occupy clusters 0, 4 and 5.
source: In contrast to Gli3 expression, Hand2 expression was not uniformly expressed, with 43% of cells expressing Hand2 occupying clusters 0,4 and 5 (Figure 2J).
evidence: The manuscript reports single-cell RNA-seq analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: 35% of Gli3+ cells also express Hand2 at E11.5.
source: scRNA-seq analyses further allowed for quantification of which NCC-cell clusters had the most robust Gli3/Hand2 co-expression. We found that 35% of Gli3+ cells also expressed Hand2 at E11.5 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The manuscript reports single-cell RNA-seq analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: 50% of Gli3+ cells in clusters 0, 4, and 5 are also Hand2+.
source: Furthermore, 50% of Gli3+ cells in cluster 0,4, and five were also Hand2+ (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The manuscript reports single-cell RNA-seq analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: 49% of cells with greater than 1.5 TPM Gli3 expression occupy clusters 0, 4, and 5.
source: While cells expressing Gli TFs did not organize to any particular clusters, 49% of cells with greater than 1.5 transcripts per million (TPM) Gli3 expression occupied clusters 0, 4, and 5.
evidence: The manuscript reports single-cell RNA-seq analysis results.

claim: 62% of cells with greater than 1.5 TPM Hand2 expression occupy clusters 0, 4, and 5.
source: Furthermore, 62% of cells with greater than 1.5 TPM Hand2 expression, also occupied clusters 0, 4, and 5 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The manuscript reports single-cell RNA-seq analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: Gene Ontology analyses for clusters 0, 4, and 5 reveal that these neural crest-derived cells contribute to skeletal and glossal development, and pattern specification.
source: Gene Ontology (GO) analyses for clusters 0, 4, and 5 revealed that these neural crest-derived cells contributed to biological processes altered in Gli2/3 cKO and Hand2 cKO mutant embryos, such as skeletal and glossal development, and pattern specification (Figure 2K).
evidence: The manuscript reports GO analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: GO-terms for phenotypes arising from dysregulation of clusters 0, 4, and 5 include 'decreased tongue size' and 'small mandible'.
source: Additionally, GO-terms for phenotypes arising from dysregulation of these cell clusters included 'decreased tongue size' and 'small mandible' (Figure 2L), suggesting that expression of Gli2/3 and Hand2 in clusters 0, 4, and five may be responsible for the phenotypes present in the conditional knockouts.
evidence: The manuscript reports GO analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: 50% of genes differentially expressed in Gli2/3 cKO MNPs are also differentially expressed in Hand2 cKO MNPs (p=3.7E-284).
source: Furthermore, hypergeometric tests revealed significant enrichment of shared transcripts. 50% of genes differentially expressed in Gli2/3 cKO MNPs were also differentially expressed in Hand2 cKO MNPs (Figure 3C, p=3.7E-284), with 29% being decreased in both mutants and 21% being increased in both mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–A').
evidence: The manuscript reports RNA-seq analysis results with statistical testing and reference to supporting figures.

claim: 29% of genes differentially expressed in both Gli2/3 cKO and Hand2 cKO MNPs are decreased in both mutants.
source: Furthermore, hypergeometric tests revealed significant enrichment of shared transcripts. 50% of genes differentially expressed in Gli2/3 cKO MNPs were also differentially expressed in Hand2 cKO MNPs (Figure 3C, p=3.7E-284), with 29% being decreased in both mutants and 21% being increased in both mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–A').
evidence: The manuscript reports RNA-seq analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: 21% of genes differentially expressed in both Gli2/3 cKO and Hand2 cKO MNPs are increased in both mutants.
source: Furthermore, hypergeometric tests revealed significant enrichment of shared transcripts. 50% of genes differentially expressed in Gli2/3 cKO MNPs were also differentially expressed in Hand2 cKO MNPs (Figure 3C, p=3.7E-284), with 29% being decreased in both mutants and 21% being increased in both mutants (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–A').
evidence: The manuscript reports RNA-seq analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: The most highly enriched TF binding site observed in Gli3 ChIP-seq on either E11.5 whole face or MNPs alone reflects the previously reported 'canonical' Gli-binding motif (cGBM) defined by the GACCACCC 8-mer.
source: As expected, the most highly enriched TF binding site observed in Gli3 ChIP-seq on either E11.5 whole face (frontonasal, maxillary and mandibular prominences) or MNPs alone reflected the previously reported 'canonical' Gli-binding motif (cGBM) defined by the GACCACCC 8-mer (Kinzler and Vogelstein, 1990; Vokes et al., 2008; Figure 3E).
evidence: The manuscript reports ChIP-seq analysis results with citations to prior work and reference to supporting figures.

claim: Hand2 peaks contain both canonical bHLH E-box motifs (CANNTG) and Hand-specific E-box motifs.
source: Similarly, Hand2 peaks contained both canonical bHLH E-box motifs (CANNTG) and Hand-specific E-box motifs (Maves et al., 2009; Kulakovskiy et al., 2013; Figure 3E).
evidence: The manuscript reports ChIP-seq analysis results with citations to prior work and reference to supporting figures.

claim: bHLH motifs are significantly enriched within Gli3 MNP peaks.
source: Further motif enrichment analyses revealed that bHLH motifs were also significantly enriched within Gli3 MNP peaks (Figure 3F).
evidence: The manuscript reports motif enrichment analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: There is a significant overlap of genomic locations occupied by Gli3 and Hand2 in the MNP (62%, 18-fold enriched, p=2.88E-213).
source: Comparison between Gli3 and Hand2 MNP ChIP-seq peaks via regulatory element locus intersection (RELI) (Harley et al., 2018) revealed a significant overlap of genomic locations occupied by Gli3 and Hand2 in the MNP (Figure 3G, 62%, 18-fold enriched, p=2.88E-213).
evidence: The manuscript reports ChIP-seq analysis results with statistical testing and reference to supporting figures.

claim: GO-terms for differentially expressed genes near Gli3 alone peaks are substantially different from GO-terms for differentially expressed genes near Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peaks.
source: Overall, the GO-terms for differentially expressed genes near Gli3 alone peaks were substantially different from the GO-terms for differentially expressed genes near Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peaks (Figure 4A).
evidence: The manuscript reports GO analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: GO-terms for differentially expressed genes near Gli3 alone peaks include pattern specification, embryonic organ development and Hh signaling.
source: Interestingly, while GO-terms for differentially expressed genes near Gli3 alone peaks included pattern specification, embryonic organ development and Hh signaling, those associated with differentially expressed genes near Gli3-Hand2 overlapping peaks included a different set of tissue-specific processes including regulation of chondrocyte differentiation and muscle cell differentiation (Figure 4A).
evidence: The manuscript reports GO analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: GO-terms for differentially expressed genes near Gli3-Hand2 overlapping peaks include regulation of chondrocyte differentiation and muscle cell differentiation.
source: Interestingly, while GO-terms for differentially expressed genes near Gli3 alone peaks included pattern specification, embryonic organ development and Hh signaling, those associated with differentially expressed genes near Gli3-Hand2 overlapping peaks included a different set of tissue-specific processes including regulation of chondrocyte differentiation and muscle cell differentiation (Figure 4A).
evidence: The manuscript reports GO analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: Approximately 337 differentially expressed genes are associated with a Gli3 alone peak.
source: While approximately 337 differentially expressed genes were associated with a Gli3 alone peak, 463 differentially expressed genes were associated with a Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peak (Figure 4B).
evidence: The manuscript reports analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: 463 differentially expressed genes are associated with a Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peak.
source: While approximately 337 differentially expressed genes were associated with a Gli3 alone peak, 463 differentially expressed genes were associated with a Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peak (Figure 4B).
evidence: The manuscript reports analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: 17% of genes with a Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peak that are increased in the Gli2/3 cKO are also increased in the Hand2 cKO.
source: 17% of genes with a Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peak that were increased in the Gli2/3 cKO, were also increased in the Hand2 cKO.
evidence: The manuscript reports analysis results.

claim: 33% of genes with a Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peak that are decreased in the Gli2/3 cKO are also decreased in the Hand2 cKO.
source: Conversely, 33% of genes with a Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peak that were decreased in the Gli2/3 cKO, were also decreased in the Hand2 cKO (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript reports analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: Gli3 and Hand2 cooperate to positively regulate genes important for mandibular development.
source: Together, these data suggested that Gli3 and Hand2 were cooperating to positively regulate genes important for mandibular development.
evidence: The manuscript interprets analysis results to infer functional relationships.

claim: Marker genes for NCC clusters have a greater association with Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peaks than Gli3 peaks alone.
source: We next superimposed E11.5 single-cell cluster markers onto these findings to reveal that marker genes for NCC clusters had a greater association with Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peaks than Gli3 peaks alone (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The manuscript reports analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: Genes that are differentially expressed in both Gli2/3 and Hand2 cKOs are more likely to be marker genes for clusters 0, 4 and 5 than marker genes for other NCC clusters or other non-NCC clusters.
source: More specifically, genes that were differentially expressed in both Gli2/3 and Hand2 cKOs were more likely to be marker genes for clusters 0, 4 and 5 than marker genes for other NCC clusters or other non-NCC clusters (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The manuscript reports analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: There is significant enrichment of cluster marker genes associated with the entire E11.5 MNP near Gli3 alone peaks.
source: While there was significant enrichment of cluster marker genes associated with the entire E11.5 MNP near Gli3 alone peaks, there was not a significant enrichment for marker genes for clusters 0, 4, 5 (Figure 4C).
evidence: The manuscript reports RELI analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: There is not a significant enrichment for marker genes for clusters 0, 4, 5 near Gli3 alone peaks.
source: While there was significant enrichment of cluster marker genes associated with the entire E11.5 MNP near Gli3 alone peaks, there was not a significant enrichment for marker genes for clusters 0, 4, 5 (Figure 4C).
evidence: The manuscript reports RELI analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: There is significant enrichment for cluster marker genes for the entire E11.5 MNP near Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peaks.
source: Interestingly, and supportive of our previous data, when we repeated this analysis for Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peaks, we found that there was significant enrichment for cluster marker genes for the entire E11.5 MNP, but also a higher enrichment for marker genes for clusters 0, 4, and 5 (Figure 4C).
evidence: The manuscript reports RELI analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: There is a higher enrichment for marker genes for clusters 0, 4, and 5 near Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peaks.
source: Interestingly, and supportive of our previous data, when we repeated this analysis for Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peaks, we found that there was significant enrichment for cluster marker genes for the entire E11.5 MNP, but also a higher enrichment for marker genes for clusters 0, 4, and 5 (Figure 4C).
evidence: The manuscript reports RELI analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: E11.5 clusters 0, 4 and 5 give rise to Myf5 and Myod1 expressing glossal musculature (clusters 1, 15, and 19) at E13.5.
source: These analyses revealed that E11.5 clusters 0, 4 and 5 gave rise to two distinct cell populations at E13.5: the Myf5 and Myod1 expressing glossal musculature (clusters 1, 15, and 19) and skeletogenic progenitors (clusters 3, 4, 5, 6, and 11), marked by many osteochondrogenic genes including Sp7, Runx2, Sox9, Col1a1, Col9a2, and Barx1.
evidence: The manuscript reports trajectory analysis results.

claim: E11.5 clusters 0, 4 and 5 give rise to skeletogenic progenitors (clusters 3, 4, 5, 6, and 11) at E13.5, marked by osteochondrogenic genes including Sp7, Runx2, Sox9, Col1a1, Col9a2, and Barx1.
source: These analyses revealed that E11.5 clusters 0, 4 and 5 gave rise to two distinct cell populations at E13.5: the Myf5 and Myod1 expressing glossal musculature (clusters 1, 15, and 19) and skeletogenic progenitors (clusters 3, 4, 5, 6, and 11), marked by many osteochondrogenic genes including Sp7, Runx2, Sox9, Col1a1, Col9a2, and Barx1.
evidence: The manuscript reports trajectory analysis results.

claim: Gli3/Hand2 interactions are enriched in E11.5 clusters 0, 4 and 5, which give rise to skeletogenic and glossal components of the lower jaw.
source: Together, these analyses suggested that Gli3/Hand2 interactions were enriched in E11.5 clusters 0, 4 and 5, which in turn give rise to skeletogenic and glossal components of the lower jaw.
evidence: The manuscript interprets analysis results to infer functional relationships.

claim: The most enriched motif within Gli3-alone peaks is the 'canonical' GBM (cGBM) defined by the 'GACCACCC' 8-mer, which is 9.8-fold-enriched compared to background sequences.
source: As expected, the most enriched motif within Gli3-alone peaks was the previously reported 'canonical' GBM (cGBM) defined by the 'GACCACCC' 8-mer (Kinzler and Vogelstein, 1990), which was 9.8-fold-enriched compared to background sequences (Figure 5A).
evidence: The manuscript reports motif analysis results with citation to prior work and reference to supporting figures.

claim: The top-ranked GBM in overlapping peaks shared between Gli3 whole face and Hand2 MNP samples deviates from the cGBM 8-mer, with reduced weight of the highly conserved 'A' at the 5th position (6.3-fold-enriched over background sequences).
source: Surprisingly, when we performed motif analysis on overlapping peaks shared between Gli3 whole face and Hand2 MNP samples, the top-ranked GBM (6.3-fold-enriched over background sequences) deviated from the cGBM 8-mer, with the most notable change being the reduced weight of the highly conserved 'A' at the 5th position (Figure 5A').
evidence: The manuscript reports motif analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: The top-ranked GBM in overlapping peaks from Gli3 and Hand2 MNP samples differs from the canonical 8-mer, having a higher probability of a 'T' rather than 'A' at the highly constrained 5th position (6.2-fold-enriched over background), designated as a 'divergent' GBM (dGBM) with the sequence GACCTCCC.
source: To specifically address the Gli3/Hand2 relationship in the MNP, we repeated these analyses using only overlapping peaks from Gli3 and Hand2 MNP samples. Here, the top-ranked GBM present (6.2-fold-enriched over background) differed even further from the canonical 8-mer, having a higher probability of either a 'T' rather than 'A' at the highly constrained 5th position (Figure 5A''). We designated this GACCTCCC 8-mer as a 'divergent' GBM (dGBM).
evidence: The manuscript reports motif analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: 85% of Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peaks contain a dGBM.
source: Interestingly, the dGBM was most clearly revealed upon comparisons between MNP data sets, with 85% of Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peaks containing dGBM and only 9% of Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peaks contained a cGBM.
evidence: The manuscript reports motif analysis results.

claim: Only 9% of Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peaks contain a cGBM.
source: Interestingly, the dGBM was most clearly revealed upon comparisons between MNP data sets, with 85% of Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peaks containing dGBM and only 9% of Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peaks contained a cGBM.
evidence: The manuscript reports motif analysis results.

claim: 6% of Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peaks contain neither a cGBM nor a dGBM.
source: 6% of Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peaks contained neither a cGBM or a dGBM (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The manuscript reports motif analysis results with reference to supporting figures.

claim: The dGBM present in MNP analysis is not present when comparing Hand2 binding in the limb.
source: Strikingly, the dGBM present in our MNP analysis was not present when comparing Hand2 binding in the limb. Rather, these analyses revealed the highly constrained 5th position remained exclusively a heavily weighted 'A'.
evidence: The manuscript reports motif analysis results comparing MNP to limb data.

claim: The dGBM utilized by Gli3 and Hand2 is specific to the MNP.
source: These data supported the possibility that the dGBM utilized by Gli3 and Hand2 was specific to the MNP.
evidence: The manuscript interprets motif analysis results to infer tissue-specificity.

claim: The consensus cGBM 8-mer (GACCACCC) is detected in 16% of Gli3-only peaks collected from the MNP.
source: While the consensus cGBM 8-mer (GACCACCC) was detected in 16% of Gli3-only peaks collected from the MNP, its occurrence was significantly reduced to only 2% of Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peaks.
evidence: The manuscript reports motif counting results.

claim: The consensus cGBM 8-mer (GACCACCC) is detected in only 2% of Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peaks.
source: While the consensus cGBM 8-mer (GACCACCC) was detected in 16% of Gli3-only peaks collected from the MNP, its occurrence was significantly reduced to only 2% of Gli3/Hand2 overlapping peaks.
evidence: The manuscript reports motif counting results.

claim: The cGBM is the 33rd most frequent 8-mer in Gli3-only MNP peaks (out of 32,896 possibilities).
source: Additionally, while the cGBM was the 33rd most frequent 8-mer in Gli3-only MNP peaks (out of 32,896 possibilities), it was 563rd in frequency in Gli3/Hand2 overlapping MNP peaks (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The manuscript reports motif counting results.

claim: The cGBM is 563rd in frequency in Gli3/Hand2 overlapping MNP peaks.
source: Additionally, while the cGBM was the 33rd most frequent 8-mer in Gli3-only MNP peaks (out of 32,896 possibilities), it was 563rd in frequency in Gli3/Hand2 overlapping MNP peaks (Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The manuscript reports motif counting results.

claim: Substitution of 'A' to 'T' in the 5th position of comparable 8-mers reduces the E-score for Gli3 binding from 0.42 to 0.33.
source: Interestingly, substitution of 'A' to 'T' in the 5th position of comparable 8-mers reduced the E-score for Gli3 binding from 0.42 to 0.33, indicating that Gli3 has a lower affinity for the dGBM sequence.
evidence: The manuscript reports PBM E-score data.

claim: Gli3 has a lower affinity for the dGBM sequence compared to the cGBM.
source: Interestingly, substitution of 'A' to 'T' in the 5th position of comparable 8-mers reduced the E-score for Gli3 binding from 0.42 to 0.33, indicating that Gli3 has a lower affinity for the dGBM sequence.
evidence: The manuscript interprets PBM E-score data to infer binding affinity.

claim: Low-affinity non-canonical GBMs with a 'T' in the 5th position regulate broad expression of Ci targets in zones of lower Hh signaling in Drosophila.
source: Likewise, previous studies in Drosophila reported that low-affinity non-canonical GBMs with a 'T' in the 5th position, similar to what we term the dGBM, were responsible for regulating broad expression of Ci targets in zones of lower Hh signaling (Parker et al., 2011).
evidence: The manuscript cites prior work in Drosophila.

claim: A single nucleotide alteration from 'A' to 'T' in the 5th position significantly decreases the affinity of Gli3 DNA binding.
source: To directly test the binding affinity of Gli3 to a dGBM, we performed gel-shift assays on synthetic sequences containing either a dGBM+E-box or cGBM+E-box. source: The Hedgehog (Hh) signaling pathway has been studied for decades in contexts ranging from organogenesis to disease (Nüsslein-Volhard and Wieschaus, 1980; Chang et al., 1994; Chiang et al., 1996; St-Jacques et al., 1999; Hebrok et al., 2000; Yao et al., 2002; Zhang et al., 2006).

claim: Transduction of the Hh pathway in mammals relies on the activity of three glioma-associated oncogene (Gli) family members Gli1, 2, and 3.
source: Transduction of the pathway in mammals relies on the activity of three glioma-associated oncogene (Gli) family members Gli1, 2, and 3, thought to be derived from duplications of a single ancestral gene similar to those found in lower chordates (Shin et al., 1999; Shimeld et al., 2007).
evidence: The manuscript provides background information with citations to prior work.

claim: Gli2 and Gli3 transcription factors function as both activators and repressors of Hh target genes.
source: While Gli2 and Gli3 transcription factors (TFs) function as both activators and repressors of Hh target genes (Dai et al., 1999; Sasaki et al., 1999; Bai et al., 2004; McDermott et al., 2005), genetic experiments have determined that Gli2 functions as the predominant activator of the pathway (Ding et al., 1998; Matise and Joyner, 1999; Park et al., 2000), whereas Gli3 functions as the predominant repressor (Persson et al., 2002).
evidence: The manuscript provides background information with citations to prior work.

claim: In the NT, Shh is produced from the ventral floor plate and forms a concentration gradient along the dorsal-ventral axis.
source: In the NT, Shh is produced from the ventral floor plate and forms a concentration gradient along the dorsal-ventral (DV) axis that is subsequently translated into a Gli activity gradient with Gli activator (GliA) levels higher ventrally and Gli repressor (GliR) levels higher dorsally (Echelard et al., 1993; Roelink et al., 1994; Briscoe and Ericson, 2001; Wijgerde et al., 2002).
evidence: The manuscript provides background information with citations to prior work.

claim: In the NT, the Shh concentration gradient is translated into a Gli activity gradient with Gli activator levels higher ventrally and Gli repressor levels higher dorsally.
source: In the NT, Shh is produced from the ventral floor plate and forms a concentration gradient along the dorsal-ventral (DV) axis that is subsequently translated into a Gli activity gradient with Gli activator (GliA) levels higher ventrally and Gli repressor (GliR) levels higher dorsally (Echelard et al., 1993; Roelink et al., 1994; Briscoe and Ericson, 2001; Wijgerde et al., 2002).
evidence: The manuscript provides background information with citations to prior work.

claim: Opposing GliA and GliR gradients in the NT correlate with Gli2 and Gli3 expression patterns, respectively, and are required for patterning motor neurons and interneurons along the DV axis.
